exposure: Mechanical ventilation (indications: severe respiratory distress, perinatal asphyxia)
Associated conditions (sepsis, respiratory distress syndrome, meconium aspiration syndrome)
cohort: 150 neonates admitted to a Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) who underwent mechanical ventilation.
finding: The predominant reason for initiating mechanical ventilation was severe respiratory distress, with sepsis being the most frequent associated condition, resulting in a survival rate of 34.66% for ventilated neonates.
